subject: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan
messages:
From: Alex Davies <alex.davies@medcore.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya R. <priya.r@medcore.com>, MedCore Legal <legal@medcore.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited about the on-prem route. Legal and procurement pushed back on two related items we need to close before signing the Order Form:

1) Operator/serviceability: they want a minimally permissive path for Redwood to assist in troubleshooting without granting full operator access. Prefer an ephemeral, auditable "read-only snapshot token" approach that lets Redwood validate model artifacts and logs during incidents.

2) Rollback/continuity guarantee: if Redwood is unable to support a private deployment (bankruptcy/exit/force majeure), MedCore needs a clear, tested transfer process for snapshots, a description of how to regenerate key material, and evidence we can restore service within an agreed RTO.

Could you send a short proposal that maps to the MSA/Order Form redlines we shared earlier? Procurement would like to see proposed contract language and any evidence artifacts (runbook, checklist) we can attach to the SOW.

—Alex
Alex Davies
Head of Cloud Ops, MedCore Health

Attachment: current_redlines_from_medcore.pdf (referenced)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Davies <alex.davies@medcore.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, MedCore Legal <legal@medcore.com>, Priya R. <priya.r@medcore.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. I'm attaching a short draft (Redwood_PrivDeploy_Guardianship_Draft_20270112.pdf) and a practical snapshot-transfer checklist. High-level takeaways we propose: 

- Ephemeral support access: we can provide time-bound, audit-logged "diagnostic tokens" scoped to read-only access of artifacts (logs, model files, runtime metrics). Token issuance requires a joint incident request (customer MAM) and is logged in the Console audit stream and in a tamper-evident delivery log.

- Snapshot transfer / recovery: we propose a two-step transfer: (1) encrypted snapshot export (customer-inserted KMS wrapping) + integrity manifest signed by Redwood, and (2) a verified restore runbook that MedCore ops executes. For escrow-like assurance, we offer a signed, time-stamped snapshot envelope plus procedural evidence (screenshot of restore run completed in staging) as an appendix to the SOW.

- Licensing boundary: model binary and weights remain under the model license in the MSA; our proposed language narrows the scope of operator actions we perform during support to diagnostic verification only. We intentionally avoid any license grant to operate on customer systems beyond the defined tokens.

Marcus — can you review the attached draft license/escrow-lite language and advise on risk? Laura — attaching runbook suggestions; please flag any operational gaps. Alex/Priya/MedCore Legal — if this aligns, we'll produce a single redline file for your counsel.

Next steps we suggest:
- Redwood: deliver redline + attachments by Jan 14
- MedCore: return comments by Jan 18
- Both: target execution of Order Form + SOW by Jan 28 (aligned with the Q1 on-prem ramp)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_PrivDeploy_Guardianship_Draft_20270112.pdf; snapshot_transfer_checklist.xlsx

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Davies <alex.davies@medcore.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, MedCore Legal <legal@medcore.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan

Vanessa / Alex — quick legal check from my side after reading the draft. High-level comments:

1) Diagnostic tokens: agree with scoped, time-bound tokens. Need to add explicit minimum authentication (mTLS + signed CSR) and an audit retention clause (we propose 12 months immutable logs for access tokens and actions). MedCore may request shorter or longer retention — flagging negotiation.

2) Snapshot transfer: the draft suggests the customer wraps the snapshot keys with customer KMS. That's good. We should add a section that clarifies Redwood does not maintain a persistent copy of customer key material post-transfer (we only hold the signed integrity manifest). Add language limiting Redwood liability where the customer fails to rotate or protect their keys after transfer.

3) Trigger for transfer: define the exact triggers (bankruptcy, failure to meet SLA for X days, insolvency, end-of-support) and require a 30-day cure opportunity where operationally possible. This avoids premature transfers.

4) Evidence artifacts: we can include a "restore run" screenshot and signed manifest as evidence in SOW Annex B. Avoid naming specific employee credentials in the runbook; reference roles and required approvals instead.

I attached a short redline of the relevant MSA clauses (inline in the PDF). Once MedCore legal agrees to the triggers and retention, we can finalize the Order Form exhibit.

—Marcus Lin
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_PrivDeploy_Guardianship_Draft_20270113_markus_redline.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Davies <alex.davies@medcore.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, MedCore Legal <legal@medcore.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 10:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan

Adding ops context and the runbook stub (operational-runbook-privdeploy-v1.2.md attached). A few operational clarifications: 

- Diagnostic token flow: token issuance will require a signed incident request email + one Richmond Ops approver approval. Token lifetime default = 4 hours, can be extended only by mutual written consent recorded in the audit log.

- Snapshot integrity: include SHA-256 manifest and a timestamped signature. We propose Redwood sign the manifest and send encrypted bundle to a mutually agreed S3 staging location; MedCore pulls and unwraps with its KMS. We can run a restore-in-staging within 5 business days of request as a one-time proof exercise at contract execution (proof-of-process).

- Offline/airgapped sites: for fully airgapped deployments we propose a signed USB image transfer protocol with chain-of-custody forms; that will be Exhibit C to the SOW.

Operational open items for procurement: who pays for a staged restore run (Redwood covers one proof-of-process; subsequent restores are billable per SOW).

Happy to sync on a short call if MedCore wants to run through the runbook.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Site Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachment: operational-runbook-privdeploy-v1.2.md; snapshot_transfer_checklist.xlsx

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Davies <alex.davies@medcore.com>, Priya R. <priya.r@medcore.com>, MedCore Legal <legal@medcore.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: serviceability & rollback guardianship plan — MAM & next steps

Alex/Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround in review. Summary and proposed mutual action plan: 

1) Redwood will issue a consolidated redline of the MSA Exhibit + Order Form language by EOD Jan 21 that incorporates Marcus's retention & triggers suggestions and Laura's operational constraints.

2) MedCore: please confirm whether the 12-month immutable audit retention is acceptable or propose an alternate retention window. Also confirm payment responsibility for extra staged restores beyond the one proof-of-process.

3) Execution milestone: target countersignature by Jan 28. If MedCore legal needs changes to the trigger language, please supply redlines by Jan 24 so both teams have time to resolve.

Finally — to make the process auditable, we'll require a Mutual Access Memo (MAM) to be attached to the Order Form whenever a diagnostic token is issued; that memo will be a short signed email stating scope, purpose, and duration and will serve as the authorization record. MedCore legal: would you be comfortable with that mechanism?

If yes, I'll prepare the redline tomorrow and route to your counsel. If you'd prefer a short call instead, I'm available Jan 22 9-11 PST.

Best,
Vanessa
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
